q: How rapidly does the observed QAOA p=1 approximation ratio on random 3-regular graphs approach the FGG'14 worst-case 0.6924 as n grows?
basis: Our small-n (6, 8, 10) sampled instances all landed at r ~ 0.82-0.85, well above the worst-case bound. The finite-size gap between typical-case and worst-case is a real quantitative object that is not mapped in the paper.
next_steps: Sweep n = 6..~200 using analytic FGG'14 per-edge formulas (which factor through pairs of edges sharing a vertex) and compare typical-case ratios of Erdos-uniformly-sampled 3-regular graphs to the 0.6924 lower bound. Cross-check a subset with direct numpy statevector at n<=20.

q: Which 3-regular graph families actually saturate the 0.6924 bound in practice?
basis: FGG'14 prove the bound but the extremal instances they cite are triangle-heavy. Our random samples had few triangles and comfortably beat 0.6924; whether triangle-density is the dominant driver of QAOA-p1 tightness is an open empirical question.
next_steps: Deterministically construct 3-regular graph families varying girth (girth 3, 4, 5, ..., >=6 Ramanujan-like) and triangle-density (triangle-free vs. triangle-dense), rerun QAOA-p1 numpy statevector, and regress r on structural features.

q: How much of the 6.1 mHa VQE-vs-literature-FCI gap is Hamiltonian coefficient truncation vs. ansatz expressivity vs. optimizer floor?
basis: Our VQE recovered the eigenvalue of the specified tapered Hamiltonian to 0.00 mHa (machine precision), but the total energy sat 6.1 mHa above the literature FCI value. Since the ansatz clearly reaches the true ground state of the given H, the gap is upper-bounded by coefficient truncation from the 4-decimal O'Malley Table I.
next_steps: Redo the Hamiltonian at full double precision using PySCF SCF + AO integrals -> parity mapping + Z2 tapering (via OpenFermion), rerun the same 6-parameter RY+CZ ansatz, and quantify the residual gap. Repeat as a function of bond length for a full dissociation curve.

q: Does the paper's D=28 entangler-depth requirement for LiH / BeH2 chemical accuracy hold when combined with modern classical optimizers (SPSA / L-BFGS-B / CMA-ES) and warm-started multi-basin search?
basis: Our H2 (D=2) VQE converged in seconds with 40 random restarts of COBYLA. That is orders of magnitude cheaper than the paper's LiH/BeH2 protocol; whether the reported D=28 is a fundamental ansatz-expressivity constraint or a search-strategy artifact is unclear from the paper.
next_steps: Extend the numpy simulator to 4/6/8-qubit tapered LiH and BeH2 Hamiltonians, sweep entangler depth D in {2,4,8,16,28} x optimizer in {COBYLA, SPSA, L-BFGS-B via parameter-shift-gradient, CMA-ES}, and plot depth vs. chemical-accuracy hit-rate.

q: At finite depth D, when does the hardware-efficient RY+CZ ansatz truly diverge from Trotterized-adiabatic QAOA on identical MaxCut instances?
basis: The paper notes the (beta_l, gamma_l) = (1-l/D, l/D) schedule makes QAOA equivalent to first-order-Trotter adiabatic evolution, but does not benchmark the two families head-to-head at finite D. Our result shows QAOA-p1 is already excellent for 3-regular MaxCut; a controlled ansatz-family comparison would clarify where hardware-efficient adds value.
next_steps: Fix a family of 3-regular MaxCut instances at n in {6,8,10,12}, sweep D in {1..10}, and compare (i) QAOA with free (beta,gamma) vs. (ii) hardware-efficient RY+CZ at matched two-qubit-gate count. Report approximation-ratio per two-qubit gate as the primary metric.
